newsitem.title: USA: CME December hogs close up sharply, at new high.
newsitem.headline: CME December hogs close up sharply, at new high.

text.p: December CME hog futures continued to show exceptional strength, with gains linked to weather and delivery concerns, traders said. Overall values in the hog pit closed mixed with December again, near its new contract high set during the session.
Pork bellies finished lower on cash belly price concerns, traders said.
December ran up to set its fresh high of 60.050 cents per lb in the closing range and ended 1.100 higher at 60.000 cents. Other months finished 0.350 cent lower to 0.125 higher.

Forcasts for bitter cold weather to sweep across Midwest hog-producing areas this week and possibly extending into next week, sparked ideas of tight market hog supplies and transportation problems, traders said.
Heavy weekend snowfall in parts of the upper Midwest followed by sharply falling temperatures kept hog shipments down Monday and cash prices ran up as much as 2.00 per cwt.
Don Roose, President of U.S. Commodities Inc attributed Monday's relatively light hog marketings to the weather.
"You can deliver hogs at a profitable level, if you can put the numbers together in a timely manner" and that was the concern driving futures up, Roose added.
